_comment: Re-extraction overlay for every money-carrying development in the corpus, keyed by record id. Answers three questions the original schema never asked: WHO is paying (government or private), WHAT the figure actually measures (a funding pot, project capex, a market aggregate, something that is not CCS funding at all), and OVER WHAT PERIOD. Applied at build time by build_dashboard.py — the underlying fact records are left untouched so the extraction stays auditable against the briefing prose it came from. Every judgement here is derived from the record's own headline and summary; where the text does not state a period, period_years is null rather than guessed.

funder_type.government: Public money — a state, region, agency or public bank is the source of funds.
funder_type.private: Company or investor money — corporate capex, venture rounds, bank facilities, supplier contracts.
funder_type.mixed: Explicitly both, with the split stated or clearly implied.
funder_type.none: No funder, because the figure is not a flow of funding at all.

basis.government-funding: A public funding commitment: grant, subsidy, contract-for-difference, tax-credit pot.
basis.private-investment: Company or investor capital going into CCS: equity, venture, debt, corporate programme.
basis.project-capex: The total build cost of a specific project. Real CCS money, but it is a cost figure, not a funding award — and the funder is often unstated.
basis.supplier-contract: Payment for goods or services within a project. Already inside somebody's capex; counting it as new money double-counts.
basis.market-aggregate: An economy-wide or sector-wide total, not a CCS commitment.
basis.not-ccs-funding: The figure is real but is not CCS funding — a legal claim, an emissions budget, a merger synergy estimate.
basis.cancelled: Money withdrawn, redirected or a project scrapped. A negative signal, never summed into positive totals.

definitions.period_years: Number of years the amount is stated to span, where the source says so. null means the source gave no period — which is the common case and is exactly why these figures must not be read as annual.
definitions.duplicate_of: This record covers the same commitment as the referenced record, or is a subset of it. Excluded from totals to prevent double-counting. The daily corpus and the GCCSI quarterly reports describe the same events in different words, so the automatic headline dedup does not catch these.

2026-06-10#02.note: Denmark's third CCS tender award to Aalborg Portland: DKK 16.5bn / €2.2bn over 15 years at €117/t for up to 1.25 Mtpa. A textbook case of a multi-year total that must not be read as a single-year figure.

2026-Q2#125.note: The same Indian CCUS scheme reported by GCCSI at the Expenditure Finance Committee stage (₹19,700 crore vs ₹20,000 crore). One scheme, two reports.

2026-Q2#64.note: INEOS/Sandpiper blue-methanol facility in Texas; FID targeted 2027, so not yet committed money.

2026-06-29#02.note: €1.2bn of a €2bn Flemish package is CCS-earmarked; €200m pre-allocated to Kairos@C, €1bn awarded competitively in 2028.

2026-Q2#109.note: EU Connecting Europe Facility call; €600m available across energy infrastructure including cross-border CO2 transport and storage — not a CCS-only pot.

2026-Q2#94.note: Eni CCUS Holding bank facility from 13 commercial lenders. Corporate debt, not public support.

2026-05-25#03.note: EU Innovation Fund Heat Auction, €400m from ETS revenues across 65 industrial heat projects. Analogous to rounds that backed Northern Lights, but this round is not CCS-specific.

2026-Q2#90.note: The €119m Votorantim award is a SUBSET of the €319m PERTE round in the record above, reported separately by GCCSI. Counting both inflates Spain.

2026-Q2#53.note: Yanchang Petroleum pipeline, CNY 1.63bn total investment.

2026-06-05#02.note: US$185m of IIJA CCS funding redirected AWAY from CCS to coal plants not required to install capture. A withdrawal of committed public money.

2026-06-03#03.note: NSW Net Zero Manufacturing round: A$225m across a scope where industrial carbon capture is one eligible category among several. Not a CCS-specific pot.

2026-Q2#56.note: SINOPEC Shengli 1 Mtpa project, CNY 920.27m total investment; construction from October 2026.

2026-Q2#114.note: Finland investment aid for biogenic CO2 capture: €90m available, €101m requested across 8 applications.

2026-07-16#01.note: UK DESNZ development-fund grant to the Viking transport & storage cluster. Note this sits INSIDE the UK's £21.7bn cluster programme — see funding-programmes.json — so it is programme drawdown, not additional money.

Carried as 'committed' in the source record, which wrongly places it in Australia's committed total — overridden to 'na' here.
